# Raspberry Pi PCF8574 I2C shift register driver for an RPLCD
# Drives digits on the RPLCD using smbus2 to send 4-bit nibbles
import smbus2
import time

# I2C address of the PCF8574 shift register on the Raspberry Pi
SHIFT_REGISTER_ADDRESS = 0x27
# RPLCD command to turn the display on
RPLCD_ON_COMMAND = 0x0C


def pulse_i2c_clock(i2c_bus, clock_bit):
    """Toggle the clock line on the I2C bus to latch a nibble."""
    # Toggle the clock bit high then low to clock the data in
    i2c_bus.write_byte(SHIFT_REGISTER_ADDRESS, clock_bit)
    time.sleep(0.0005)
    i2c_bus.write_byte(SHIFT_REGISTER_ADDRESS, (clock_bit | 0x04) & 0xFF)
    time.sleep(0.0001)
    i2c_bus.write_byte(SHIFT_REGISTER_ADDRESS, (clock_bit & ~0x04))


def write_byte(i2c_bus, value, mode):
    """Write a byte to the RPLCD using four 4-bit nibbles."""
    # Split the byte into high and low nibbles for the display
    high_nibble = mode | (value & 0xF0) | 0x08 | 0x00
    low_nibble = mode | ((value << 4) & 0xF0) | 0x08 | 0x00
    for nibble_value in (high_nibble, low_nibble):
        pulse_i2c_clock(i2c_bus, nibble_value)


def main():
    """Drive the RPLCD with a repeating sequence of digits."""
    # Open the I2C bus that the PCF8574 is wired to
    i2c_bus = smbus2.SMBus(1)
    try:
        # Send the on command and a few status bytes
        write_byte(i2c_bus, RPLCD_ON_COMMAND, 0x00)
        write_byte(i2c_bus, 0x06, 0x00)
        write_byte(i2c_bus, 0x01, 0x00)
        for digit_value in range(4):
            write_byte(i2c_bus, digit_value, 0x00)
            time.sleep(0.5)
    except OSError as bus_error:
        # Report any I2C communication failure
        print("I2C error:", bus_error)
    finally:
        # Close the I2C bus to release the device
        i2c_bus.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Reads a single channel and prints the 10-bit result on stdout
import time
import logging
import sys

# Configure logging for the ADS1115 reader
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(message)s")

# ADS1115 I2C address and device class for the Raspberry Pi
ADS1115_ADDRESS = 0x48
ADS1115_DEVICE = 0
CONTINUOUS_MODE = 0x85


def read_channel(adc_device):
    """Read a single channel from the ADS1115 and return the 10-bit value."""
    # Start continuous conversion and wait for the result
    adc_device.start_conversion(CONTINUOUS_MODE)
    while adc_device.is_conversion_done() == 0:
        time.sleep(0.01)
    raw_value = adc_device.read_adc(0, gain=1)
    return raw_value


def main():
    """Open the ADS1115 and sample the channel repeatedly."""
    adc_device = None
    try:
        # Open the I2C device and read a few channels
        logging.info("Starting ADS1115 ADC reader")
        adc_device = adafruit_ads1x15.ADS1115(address=ADS1115_ADDRESS, busnum=1)
        for sample_index in range(10):
            channel_value = read_channel(adc_device)
            if channel_value > 2047:
                channel_value -= 4095
            print("ADC channel %d=%d" % (0, channel_value))
            time.sleep(0.1)
    except OSError as sensor_error:
        # Report a missing or busy device
        logging.error("ADC error: %s", sensor_error)
        sys.stderr.write("Failed to read ADC\n")
    except Exception as read_error:
        # Catch any other failure during sampling
        logging.error("Sampling error: %s", read_error)
    finally:
        # Always release the ADC device
        if adc_device is not None:
            adc_device.close()
        logging.info("ADC reader stopped")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# MPU6050 orientation sensor reader for Raspberry Pi
# Reads accelerometer and gyroscope data over I2C using smbus2
import smbus2
import time

# MPU6050 I2C address and bus number on the Raspberry Pi
MPU6050_ADDRESS = 0x68
I2C_BUS_NUMBER = 1
READ_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 0.01


def read_raw_word(i2c_bus, register_address):
    """Read a 16-bit raw word from two consecutive registers."""
    # Combine the high and low bytes into a single 16-bit value
    high_byte = i2c_bus.read_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, register_address)
    low_byte = i2c_bus.read_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, register_address + 1)
    raw_value = (high_byte << 8) | low_byte
    return raw_value


def read_orientation(i2c_bus):
    """Read and print the current orientation in degrees."""
    # Read the accelerometer and gyroscope axes
    accel_x = read_raw_word(i2c_bus, 0x3B)
    accel_y = read_raw_word(i2c_bus, 0x3D)
    gyro_x = read_raw_word(i2c_bus, 0x43)
    gyro_y = read_raw_word(i2c_bus, 0x45)
    # Convert raw counts to approximate degrees per second
    accel_angle = 131.0 * gyro_x / 131.0
    gyro_angle = 131.0 * gyro_y / 131.0
    print("Accel X=%.0f deg/s, Y=%.0f deg/s" % (accel_x, gyro_angle))
    return accel_angle


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Open the I2C bus and read the MPU6050 orientation sensor
    i2c_bus = smbus2.SMBus(I2C_BUS_NUMBER)
    try:
        for sample_index in range(10):
            orientation_value = read_orientation(i2c_bus)
            time.sleep(READ_INTERVAL_SECONDS)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("Stopped by user")
    except Exception as sensor_error:
        # Report any I2C communication failure
        print("Sensor error:", sensor_error)
    finally:
        # Close the I2C bus to release the hardware
        i2c_bus.close()

    """Open and configure the SPI bus for the MCP3008 ADC."""
    # Create the SPI device used by the MCP3008 chip

    adc_bus.open(0, 0)

    # Build the three-byte command for a single-ended read
    command_bytes = [1, (8 + channel_number) << 4, 0]
    response_bytes = adc_bus.xfer2(command_bytes)
    # Combine the response bytes into a single 10-bit number
    raw_value = ((response_bytes[1] & 3) << 8) + response_bytes[2]
    return raw_value


def main():

            if raw_value > 1023:

import time

# MPU6050 I2C address and register map
MPU6050_ADDRESS = 0x68
POWER_MGMT_REGISTER = 0x6B
ACCEL_XOUT_HIGH = 0x3B
GYRO_XOUT_HIGH = 0x43


def read_word(bus_handle, register_address):
    """Read a 16-bit signed value from two consecutive registers."""
    # Combine the high and low bytes into a single signed integer
    high_byte = bus_handle.read_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, register_address)
    low_byte = bus_handle.read_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, register_address + 1)
    raw_value = (high_byte << 8) | low_byte
    if raw_value >= 0x8000:
        raw_value -= 0x10000
    return raw_value


def main():
    """Continuously read and print MPU6050 orientation data."""
    bus_handle = smbus2.SMBus(1)
    try:
        # Wake the MPU6050 from sleep mode
        bus_handle.write_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, POWER_MGMT_REGISTER, 0)
        for sample_index in range(10):
            accel_x = read_word(bus_handle, ACCEL_XOUT_HIGH)
            gyro_x = read_word(bus_handle, GYRO_XOUT_HIGH)
            print("Accel X:", accel_x, "G, Gyro X:", gyro_x, "DPS")
            time.sleep(0.05)
    except OSError:
        print("MPU6050 not found on I2C bus")
    finally:
        # Close the I2C bus handle
        bus_handle.close()

# Raspberry Pi camera capture for an industrial automation station
# Captures a single image and saves it to disk using picamera2
import time
import logging
from picamera2 import Picamera2

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)

def configure_camera():
    """Create and start a picamera2 instance for still capture."""
    # Build a still configuration and attach it to the camera
    camera_device = Picamera2()
    still_config = camera_device.create_still_configuration()
    camera_device.configure(still_config)
    camera_device.start()
    return camera_device

def capture_image(camera_device, output_path):
    """Capture one image and write it to the given path."""
    # Capture the image and return the filename if successful
    image_file = camera_device.capture_file(output_path)
    if image_file is None:
        return False
    logging.info("Saved image to %s", output_path)
    return True

def run_capture_loop(camera_device, total_frames, interval_seconds):
    """Capture a fixed number of frames at a given interval."""
    # Loop until the requested number of frames is captured
    frame_count = 0
    while frame_count < total_frames:
        if capture_image(camera_device, "captured_%03d.jpg" % frame_count):
            frame_count += 1
        time.sleep(interval_seconds)
    return frame_count

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Capture a short video stream for quality control
    camera_capture = configure_camera()
    try:
        captured_frames = run_capture_loop(camera_capture, 5, 2)
    except Exception as capture_error:
        logging.error("Capture failed: %s", capture_error)
    finally:
        # Stop the camera and release the device
        camera_capture.stop()

# MPU6050 orientation sensor reader for Raspberry Pi
# Reads accelerometer and gyroscope axes over I2C using smbus2
import smbus2
import time

# MPU6050 I2C address and register map
MPU6050_ADDRESS = 0x68
POWER_MGMT_REGISTER = 0x6B
ACCEL_XOUT_REGISTER = 0x3B
GYRO_XOUT_REGISTER = 0x43


def read_axis(bus_handle, register_address):
    """Read a signed 16-bit value from one MPU6050 register."""
    # Combine the high and low bytes into a signed integer
    high_byte = bus_handle.read_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, register_address)
    low_byte = bus_handle.read_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, register_address + 1)
    raw_value = (high_byte << 8) | low_byte
    if raw_value >= 0x8000:
        raw_value -= 0x10000
    return raw_value


def main():
    # Open the I2C bus that the MPU6050 is connected to
    i2c_bus = smbus2.SMBus(1)
    try:
        # Wake the MPU6050 from sleep mode
        i2c_bus.write_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, POWER_MGMT_REGISTER, 0)
        # Read the accelerometer and gyroscope axes
        accel_x = read_axis(i2c_bus, ACCEL_XOUT_REGISTER)
        gyro_x = read_axis(i2c_bus, GYRO_XOUT_REGISTER)
        # Print the orientation values in degrees per second
        print("Accel X:", accel_x, "deg/s")
        print("Gyro X:", gyro_x, "deg/s")
    except OSError:
        # The MPU6050 is not wired or powered up
        print("MPU6050 not found")
    finally:
        # Close the I2C bus handle
        i2c_bus.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Raspberry Pi camera capture for a smart retail display
# Uses picamera2 to grab a single image and save it to disk
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

# Configure the Raspberry Pi camera for still capture
def configure_camera():
    """Create and start a picamera2 instance for still capture."""
    # Build a still configuration for the Raspberry Pi camera
    camera_config = Picamera2().create_still_configuration()
    # Apply the configuration to the camera hardware
    camera_handle = Picamera2(camera_config)
    # Start the camera so it is ready to capture
    camera_handle.start()
    return camera_handle

# Capture one image and save it to a file
def capture_image(camera_handle, output_path):
    """Capture a single image and write it to the given path."""
    # Capture the image to a byte buffer
    image_buffer = camera_handle.capture_array()
    # Save the buffer to a file
    with open(output_path, "wb") as output_file:
        output_file.write(image_buffer)

# Main entry point for the retail display capture loop
def run_capture_loop(camera_handle, output_path, interval_seconds):
    """Capture a loop of images at a given interval."""
    # Capture one image per interval
    for capture_index in range(5):
        capture_image(camera_handle, output_path)
        print("Captured retail image", capture_index)
        # Wait before the next capture
        time.sleep(interval_seconds)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Retail display capture target path
    capture_target = "retail_display_capture.jpg"
    # Capture loop interval in seconds
    capture_interval = 0.5
    # Build the camera instance
    retail_camera = configure_camera()
    try:
        # Run the capture loop
        run_capture_loop(retail_camera, capture_target, capture_interval)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        # Stop capture on user interrupt
        print("Capture stopped")
    finally:
        # Release the camera hardware
        retail_camera.stop()

# BME280 environmental sensor reader for Raspberry Pi
# Reads a temperature and pressure measurement over I2C
import smbus2
import time

# I2C address of the BME280 sensor module
BME280_ADDRESS = 0x29
# Register where the measurement registers start
MEASURE_REG = 0xF7

def read_raw_word(i2c_bus, register):
    """Read a 16-bit word from two consecutive registers."""
    # Combine the high and low bytes from the register
    high_byte = i2c_bus.read_byte_data(BME280_ADDRESS, register)
    low_byte = i2c_bus.read_byte_data(BME280_ADDRESS, register + 1)
    raw_value = (high_byte << 8) | low_byte
    return raw_value

def read_bme280(i2c_bus):
    """Read the temperature and pressure from the BME280."""
    # Read the raw pressure and temperature registers
    raw_pressure = read_raw_word(i2c_bus, MEASURE_REG)
    raw_temperature = read_raw_word(i2c_bus, MEASURE_REG + 4)
    # Apply the calibration factors from the datasheet
    pressure_hpa = 1048576.0 - raw_pressure
    temperature_celsius = 27.0 + (raw_temperature / 100.0)
    return pressure_hpa, temperature_celsius

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Open the I2C bus on the Raspberry Pi
    i2c_bus = smbus2.SMBus(1)
    try:
        # Continuously sample the sensor
        while True:
            pressure_hpa, temperature_celsius = read_bme280(i2c_bus)
            print("Pressure: {0:.2f} hPa Temperature: {1:.2f} C".format(pressure_hpa, temperature_celsius))
            time.sleep(2)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        # Stop reading on user interrupt
        print("Stopping BME280 reader")
    finally:
        # Release the I2C bus on exit
        i2c_bus.close()

# SPI channel wired to the MCP3008 ADC

SPI_BUS = 0
SPI_DEVICE = 0


def open_adc():
    """Open and configure the MCP3008 ADC over SPI."""
    # Create the SPI device used by the MCP3008 chip

    command_bytes = [1, (8 + channel_number) << 4, 0]
    response_bytes = adc_bus.xfer2(command_bytes)
    # Combine the response bytes into a single integer value
    raw_value = ((response_bytes[1] & 3) << 8) + response_bytes[2]
    return raw_value

import spidev

SPI_BUS = 0
SPI_DEVICE = 0


def open_adc():
    """Open and configure the MCP3008 ADC over SPI."""

    adc_device = spidev.SpiDev()
    adc_device.open(SPI_BUS, SPI_DEVICE)

    command_frame = [1, (8 + channel_number) << 4, 0]
    response_bytes = adc_device.xfer2(command_frame)
    # Combine the two response bytes into a single integer
    raw_value = ((response_bytes[1] & 3) << 8) + response_bytes[2]

# Drives an HD44780 character display with RPLCD over GPIO
import RPi.GPIO as GPIO
import time

# GPIO pins for the HD44780 data lines
DATA_PIN = 26
CLOCK_PIN = 19
LATCH_PIN = 20

# Display columns and row addressing
DISPLAY_WIDTH = 16
DISPLAY_ROWS = 2
DISPLAY_CHAR_COUNT = DISPLAY_ROWS * DISPLAY_WIDTH

# Initialize the HD44780 display
def init_display():
    """Configure the HD44780 pins and enter 4-bit mode."""
    # Set all pins as outputs
    GPIO.setmode(GPIO.BCM)
    GPIO.setup(DATA_PIN, GPIO.OUT)
    GPIO.setup(CLOCK_PIN, GPIO.OUT)
    GPIO.setup(LATCH_PIN, GPIO.OUT)
    # Initialise the controller into 4-bit mode
    send_nibble(0x33, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x20, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x0C, 0x07)
    send_nibble(0x28, 0x03)
    send_nibble(0x01, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x06, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x09, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x0C, 0x07)
    send_nibble(0x14, 0x01)
    send_nibble(0x15, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x40, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x50, 0x3F)
    send_nibble(0x90, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x24, 0x0F)
    send_nibble(0x25, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x2A, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x2B, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x2C, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x2D, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x2E, 0x00)
    send_nibble(0x00, 0x00)

# Send a single nibble to the display
def send_nibble(nibble_value, mode_value):
    """Shift out a nibble to the data pin with the given mode bit."""
    GPIO.output(LATCH_PIN, GPIO.LOW)
    GPIO.output(CLOCK_PIN, GPIO.LOW)
    GPIO.output(DATA_PIN, (nibble_value & 0xF0) | mode_value)
    GPIO.output(CLOCK_PIN, GPIO.HIGH)
    GPIO.output(CLOCK_PIN, GPIO.LOW)
    GPIO.output(DATA_PIN, (nibble_value << 4) & 0xF0)
    GPIO.output(CLOCK_PIN, GPIO.HIGH)
    GPIO.output(CLOCK_PIN, GPIO.LOW)
    GPIO.output(LATCH_PIN, GPIO.HIGH)

# Send a block of bytes to the display
def send_block(block_data):
    """Shift out a block of bytes to the display data register."""
    for byte_value in block_data:
        send_nibble(byte_value, 0x00)

# Write a string to the display
def write_string(text_value):
    """Encode each character into a block of bytes and push it to the display."""
    for character in text_value:
        char_code = ord(character)
        send_nibble(char_code & 0xF0, 0x00)
        char_code = (char_code << 4) & 0xF0
        send_nibble(char_code | 0x0F, 0x00)

# Display a single value on the HD44780
def display_value(value_text, value_int):
    """Write a value and its text label to the HD44780 display."""
    write_string(value_text + " " + str(value_int))
    time.sleep(1)

# Main loop for the HD44780 display

        # Initialise the HD44780 display
        init_display()

    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        # Stop the display loop on interrupt
        print("Display stopped")
    finally:
        # Release the HD44780 GPIO pins
        GPIO.cleanup()

    # Apply the calibration scale factors from the datasheet
    pressure_hpa = pressure_raw / 100.0
    temperature_celsius = temperature_raw / 100.0
    humidity_percent = humidity_raw / 100.0
    return temperature_celsius, humidity_percent, pressure_hpa

    raw_bytes = i2c_bus.read_i2c_block_data(SENSOR_ADDRESS, DATA_REGISTER, 2)

import time

    i2c_bus.write_byte(BMP280_ADDRESS, 0xF7)
    time.sleep(0.05)
    raw_bytes = i2c_bus.read_i2c_block_data(BMP280_ADDRESS, 0x88, 3)
    raw_pressure = (raw_bytes[0] << 12) | (raw_bytes[1] << 4) | (raw_bytes[2] >> 4)
    # Apply the sensor's scaling factor to get hPa
    pressure_hpa = 1048576.0 - raw_pressure
    return round(pressure_hpa, 2)

def main():

    try:
        for reading_index in range(2):

            print("Pressure reading", reading_index, "hPa", pressure_value)
            time.sleep(1)
    except OSError:
        print("BMP280 sensor not found on I2C bus")

import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)

# MCP3008 channel wired to the potentiometer
POT_CHANNEL = 0
# SPI bus and device numbers for the ADC
SPI_BUS = 0
SPI_DEVICE = 0


def read_adc_channel(channel_number):
    """Read a single MCP3008 channel and return its 10-bit value."""
    # Build the SPI command frame for the requested channel
    command_frame = [1, (8 + channel_number) << 4, 0]
    response_bytes = SPI_BUS, SPI_DEVICE, command_frame
    # Transfer the command and read the 12-bit response
    response_bytes = read_spi_block(response_bytes)
    # Combine the two response bytes into a 10-bit value
    raw_value = (response_bytes[1] << 8) | response_bytes[2]
    return raw_value


def read_spi_block(command_frame):
    """Send a single SPI command and return the response bytes."""
    # Transfer the command frame to the MCP3008
    for command, value in command_frame:
        send_spi_command(command, value)
    # Wait for the ADC to settle before reading
    time.sleep(0.0005)
    response_bytes = []
    for i in range(3):
        send_spi_command(0x01, 0x08)
        response_bytes.append(read_spi_block([0])[0])
    return response_bytes


def send_spi_command(command, value):
    """Send a single SPI command byte to the MCP3008."""
    # The MCP3008 expects a single command byte per transfer
    SPI_BUS, SPI_DEVICE, _ = read_spi_block([0])
    SPI_BUS, SPI_DEVICE, command_frame = SPI_BUS, SPI_DEVICE, [command, value]
    send_spi_command(command_frame[0], command_frame[1])

    spi_bus = None
    try:

        raw_value = read_adc_channel(POT_CHANNEL)

        # Report any SPI read failure

# Drives an HD44780 character display with RPLCD over GPIO
import RPi.GPIO as GPIO
import time

# GPIO pins for the HD44780 data lines
DATA_PIN = 26
CLOCK_PIN = 19
LATCH_PIN = 20

# Display columns and row addresses
COLUMN_ADDR = 0x00
ROW_ADDR = 0x01
MODE_SET = 0x02
DATA_MODE = 0x04
CHAR_SET = 0x08


def pulse_clock(clock_pin, data_pin, latch_pin, bit_number):
    """Toggle the clock line to latch a nibble into the display."""
    # Clock the data bit in and out with a short delay
    GPIO.output(clock_pin, GPIO.LOW)
    time.sleep(0.0005)
    GPIO.output(clock_pin, GPIO.HIGH)
    time.sleep(0.0005)
    GPIO.output(clock_pin, GPIO.LOW)
    time.sleep(0.0005)
    GPIO.output(latch_pin, GPIO.HIGH)


def write_byte(data_pin, clock_pin, latch_pin, value):
    """Write a byte to the display as four 4-bit nibbles."""
    # Split the byte into high and low nibbles
    high_nibble = (value >> 4) & 0x0F
    low_nibble = (value << 4) & 0xF0
    for nibble_value in (high_nibble, low_nibble):
        for bit_number in range(8):
            pulse_clock(clock_pin, GPIO.HIGH, latch_pin, bit_number)


def display_text(data_pin, clock_pin, latch_pin, text_value):
    """Send each character of the text to the HD44780 display."""
    # Send each character as a 4-bit nibble
    for character in text_value:
        char_code = ord(character)
        write_byte(data_pin, clock_pin, latch_pin, char_code)

    GPIO.setmode(GPIO.BCM)
    GPIO.setup(DATA_PIN, GPIO.OUT)
    GPIO.setup(CLOCK_PIN, GPIO.OUT)
    GPIO.setup(LATCH_PIN, GPIO.OUT)

# Reads current and voltage from the chip and reports the result
import time
import smbus2

INA219_ADDRESS = 0x40
I2C_BUS_NUMBER = 1
READ_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 2


def read_ina219(i2c_bus, device_address):
    """Read the current and voltage from the INA219 over I2C."""
    # Trigger a measurement and read the resulting bytes
    i2c_bus.write_i2c_block_data(device_address, 0x02, [0x83, 0xE0])
    time.sleep(0.05)
    raw_bytes = i2c_bus.read_i2c_block_data(device_address, 0x00, 2)
    raw_value = (raw_bytes[0] << 8) | raw_bytes[1]
    voltage_millivolts = (raw_value / 1000.0) * 4.096
    current_milliamps = (raw_value / 1000.0) * 0.001
    return voltage_millivolts, current_milliamps


def main():
    """Continuously read the INA219 and report the result."""
    i2c_bus = smbus2.SMBus(I2C_BUS_NUMBER)
    try:
        # Sample the measurement station a few times
        for sample_index in range(5):
            voltage_millivolts, current_milliamps = read_ina219(i2c_bus, INA219_ADDRESS)
            print("Sample", sample_index, "millivolts", voltage_millivolts, "milliamps", current_milliamps)
            time.sleep(READ_INTERVAL_SECONDS)
    except OSError as bus_error:
        # Report a missing or unresponsive INA219
        print("INA219 not found:", bus_error)
    finally:
        # Close the I2C bus on exit
        i2c_bus.close()

# Reads accelerometer and gyroscope over I2C using smbus2
import smbus2
import time

# MPU6050 I2C address and measurement register
MPU6050_ADDRESS = 0x68
POWER_MGMT_REGISTER = 0x6B
ACCEL_XOUT_HIGH = 0x3B
GYRO_XOUT_HIGH = 0x43


def read_word(bus_handle, register_address):
    """Read a 16-bit signed value from two consecutive registers."""
    # Combine the high and low bytes into a signed integer
    high_byte = bus_handle.read_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, register_address)
    low_byte = bus_handle.read_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, register_address + 1)
    raw_value = (high_byte << 8) + low_byte
    if raw_value >= 0x8000:
        raw_value -= 0x10000
    return raw_value


def read_orientation(bus_handle):
    """Read and print the accelerometer and gyroscope values."""
    # Read the accelerometer and gyroscope registers
    accel_x = read_word(bus_handle, ACCEL_XOUT_HIGH)
    accel_y = read_word(bus_handle, ACCEL_XOUT_HIGH + 2)
    accel_z = read_word(bus_handle, ACCEL_XOUT_HIGH + 4)
    gyro_x = read_word(bus_handle, GYRO_XOUT_HIGH)
    gyro_y = read_word(bus_handle, GYRO_XOUT_HIGH + 2)
    gyro_z = read_word(bus_handle, GYRO_XOUT_HIGH + 4)
    print("Accel X=%.0f, Y=%.0f, Z=%.0f g" % (accel_x, accel_y, accel_z))
    print("Gyro X=%.0f, Y=%.0f, Z=%.0f deg/s" % (gyro_x, gyro_y, gyro_z))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Open the I2C bus and read the MPU6050 once
    bus_handle = smbus2.SMBus(1)
    try:
        bus_handle.write_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, POWER_MGMT_REGISTER, 0)
        read_orientation(bus_handle)
    except OSError:
        print("MPU6050 not found on I2C bus")
    finally:
        # Close the I2C bus on exit
        bus_handle.close()

# Raspberry Pi analog input reader for a clean energy monitoring node
# Reads an MCP3008 ADC over SPI using the adafruit-circuitpython-mcp3xxx driver
import time
import logging
import sys
from datetime import datetime

# Configure logging for the clean energy monitoring node
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(message)s")

# SPI channel and device used by the MCP3008 ADC
ADC_CHANNEL = 0
ADC_DEVICE = 0


def read_adc_channel(adc_device, channel_number):
    """Read a single 10-bit value from one MCP3008 ADC channel."""
    # Build the SPI command frame for the requested channel
    command_frame = [1, (8 + channel_number) << 4, 0]
    response_bytes = spi_transfer(command_frame)
    # Combine the two response bytes into a single 10-bit value
    raw_value = (response_bytes[0] << 8) | response_bytes[1]
    return raw_value


def spi_transfer(command_frame):
    """Send a SPI command frame and return the response bytes."""
    # Use the RPi.GPIO SPI interface for the MCP3008
    import RPi.GPIO as GPIO
    GPIO.setmode(GPIO.BCM)
    GPIO.setup(adc_device, GPIO.OUT)
    GPIO.output(adc_device, command_frame[0])
    time.sleep(0.0005)
    GPIO.setup(adc_device, GPIO.IN)
    response_bytes = []
    for i in range(command_frame[2]):
        GPIO.setup(adc_device, GPIO.OUT)
        GPIO.output(adc_device, 0)
        time.sleep(0.0005)
        GPIO.setup(adc_device, GPIO.IN)
        response_bytes.append(GPIO.input(adc_device))
    return response_bytes


def main():
    """Continuously sample the analog channel and report readings."""
    spi_device = 0
    try:
        # Open the SPI bus to the MCP3008 ADC
        spi_bus = GPIO.SpiDev()
        spi_bus.open(spi_device, ADC_DEVICE)
        spi_bus.max_speed_hz = 1350000
        for sample_index in range(10):
            raw_value = read_adc_channel(spi_device, ADC_CHANNEL)
            # Reject readings that fail the CRC check
            if raw_value > 32767 or raw_value < 0:
                logging.warning("Invalid ADC reading: %d", raw_value)
                continue
            stamp = datetime.now().isoformat()
            logging.info("%s -> %d", stamp, raw_value)
            time.sleep(2)
    except Exception as error:
        # Report any SPI or device failure
        logging.error("ADC error: %s", error)
    finally:
        # Always release the SPI bus on exit
        spi_bus.close()
        sys.exit(0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import smbus2

# I2C address and bus number for the MPU6050
MPU6050_ADDRESS = 0x68
I2C_BUS_NUMBER = 1
READ_COUNT = 8
READ_INTERVAL = 0.1


def read_raw_word(i2c_bus, register_address):
    """Read a 16-bit word from two consecutive registers."""
    # Combine the high and low bytes into a single value
    high_byte = i2c_bus.read_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, register_address)
    low_byte = i2c_bus.read_byte_data(MPU6050_ADDRESS, register_address + 1)
    raw_value = (high_byte << 8) | low_byte
    return raw_value


def read_gyroscope(i2c_bus):

    # Read the six gyroscope axes and convert to signed values
    rate_x = read_raw_word(i2c_bus, 0x03) * 0.0039
    rate_y = read_raw_word(i2c_bus, 0x05) * 0.0039
    rate_z = read_raw_word(i2c_bus, 0x07) * 0.0039
    return rate_x, rate_y, rate_z


def main():

    i2c_bus = smbus2.SMBus(I2C_BUS_NUMBER)
    try:
        for reading_index in range(READ_COUNT):
            rate_x, rate_y, rate_z = read_gyroscope(i2c_bus)
            # Print each reading with a short delay
            print("gyro X: %.3f, Y: %.3f, Z: %.3f" % (rate_x, rate_y, rate_z))

        i2c_bus.close()

BME280_ADDRESS = 0x76
I2C_BUS_NUMBER = 1
READ_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 2
READ_TOTAL = 5


def read_bme280_data(i2c_bus):
    """Read raw temperature, humidity and pressure bytes from the sensor."""
    # Trigger a measurement and read the three 2-byte registers
    raw_bytes = i2c_bus.read_i2c_block_data(BME280_ADDRESS, 0xF7, 6)
    pressure_raw = (raw_bytes[0] << 12) | (raw_bytes[1] << 4)
    temperature_raw = (raw_bytes[2] << 12) | (raw_bytes[3] << 4)
    humidity_raw = (raw_bytes[4] << 8) | raw_bytes[5]

def convert_units(temperature_raw, pressure_raw, humidity_raw):
    """Convert raw sensor values into engineering units."""
    # Apply the datasheet conversion factors
    temperature_c = 15.0 + (temperature_raw / 100.0)
    pressure_hpa = pressure_raw / 100.0
    humidity_percent = humidity_raw / 100.0
    return temperature_c, pressure_hpa, humidity_percent

    i2c_bus = smbus2.SMBus(I2C_BUS_NUMBER)
    try:

# Reads an MCP3008 ADC over SPI using the adafruit-circuitpython-mcp3xxx driver
import time
import logging
import spidev

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)

# SPI channel and device for the MCP3008 ADC
ADC_CHANNEL = 0
SPI_BUS = 0
SPI_DEVICE = 0


def open_adc():
    """Open and configure the SPI ADC device."""
    # Create the SPI connection to the MCP3008 chip
    adc_bus = spidev.SpiDev()
    adc_bus.open(SPI_BUS, SPI_DEVICE)
    adc_bus.max_speed_hz = 1350000
    return adc_bus


def read_adc_channel(adc_bus, channel_number):
    """Read a single 10-bit value from one ADC channel."""
    # Build the three-byte command for the requested channel
    command_bytes = [1, (8 + channel_number) << 4, 0]
    response_bytes = adc_bus.xfer2(command_bytes)
    # Combine the response bytes into a single integer
    raw_value = ((response_bytes[1] & 3) << 8) + response_bytes[2]
    return raw_value


def main():
    """Continuously sample the analog input and print the reading."""
    adc_bus = open_adc()
    try:
        # Sample the channel repeatedly while the node runs
        while True:
            raw_reading = read_adc_channel(adc_bus, ADC_CHANNEL)
            if raw_reading > 1023:
                raw_reading -= 4096
            print("ADC channel", ADC_CHANNEL, "raw", raw_reading)
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        logging.info("Sampling stopped by operator")
    except Exception as error:
        logging.error("ADC read failed: %s", error)
    finally:
        # Close the SPI device to release the hardware
        adc_bus.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import time

# I2C address of the ADXL345 accelerometer
ADXL345_ADDRESS = 0x1d
# Register where the accelerometer data begins
DATA_X_LSB = 0x32

def read_axis(bus_handle, register):
    """Read a signed 16-bit axis value from the accelerometer."""
    # Read two bytes and combine them into a signed value
    high_byte = bus_handle.read_byte_data(ADXL345_ADDRESS, register)
    low_byte = bus_handle.read_byte_data(ADXL345_ADDRESS, register + 1)
    raw_value = (high_byte << 8) | low_byte
    if raw_value >= 0x8000:
        raw_value -= 0x10000
    return raw_value

def main():
    """Continuously read and print the accelerometer axes."""
    bus_handle = smbus2.SMBus(1)
    try:
        while True:
            # Read each axis and print the reading
            x_value = read_axis(bus_handle, DATA_X_LSB)
            y_value = read_axis(bus_handle, DATA_X_LSB + 2)
            z_value = read_axis(bus_handle, DATA_X_LSB + 4)
            print("X=%.0f, Y=%.0f, Z=%.0f" % (x_value, y_value, z_value))
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:

        bus_handle.close()

    main()
